2607.28527.title: MANTA: Multi-Agent Network Topology Adaptation for Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Systems
2607.28527.paper_summary: Large language model-based multi-agent systems improve complex problem solving through task decomposition, agent specialization, information exchange, and intermediate validation. However, existing systems typically treat communication topology as a fixed design choice or an offline optimization target. We introduce MANTA, a framework for Multi-Agent Network Topology Adaptation that enables communication structures to self-evolve at inference time. Before execution, MANTA initializes a task-conditioned topology from prior structural experience. During deployment, it monitors collaboration traces and applies bounded structural updates when the current organization becomes insufficient. These updates can modify agent roles, communication links, execution order, information visibility, and validation pathways while preserving the task interface and agent budget. We evaluate MANTA against representative single-agent and multi-agent baselines on five benchmarks spanning information seeking, tool use, planning, workflow execution, and mathematical reasoning. MANTA achieves the highest average score of 74.0, outperforming the strongest baseline by 5.8 percentage points and obtaining the best result on PlanCraft. These results show that inference-time self-improvement can extend to the architecture of collaboration itself.
2607.28527.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型基礎的多智能體系統透過任務分解、智能體專業化、信息交換和中介驗證來改善複雜問題的解決。然而，現有系統通常將通信拓撲視為固定的設計選擇或離線優化目標。我們介紹了MANTA，一個多智能體網絡拓撲適應框架，該框架使通信結構能夠在推理時自我演變。在執行之前，MANTA根據先前的結構經驗初始化一個任務條件拓撲。在部署期間，它監控協作痕跡，並在當前組織變得不足時應用有界結構更新。這些更新可以修改智能體角色、通信連結、執行順序、信息可見性和驗證路徑，同時保留任務介面和智能體預算。我們在五個基準上評估MANTA，這些基準涵蓋信息搜尋、工具使用、規劃、工作流程執行和數學推理，並與代表性的單智能體和多智能體基準進行比較。MANTA達到了74.0的最高平均分，超越了最強基準5.8個百分點，並在PlanCraft上獲得了最佳結果。這些結果表明，推理時的自我改進可以擴展到協作架構本身。
